title: How pigeons find their way home
topic: How do pigeons find their way home?

lines: What lets a pigeon sprint 100 miles straight back home?

beats.title: Sun compass
lines: They read the bright sun’s position like a built‑in clock.
By shifting their internal clock they keep the sun’s angle precisely correct.
When clouds hide the sun, a tiny magnet in their nasal cavity takes over.
Researchers attached a small magnet and saw the birds veer off, proving a magnetic compass linked to the trigeminal nerve.

beats.title: Smell & sight
lines: They also sniff familiar city smells and match streets they’ve seen before.
Visual landmarks let them make right‑angle turns along familiar routes.
Next time you see a pigeon, watch it turn toward home quickly even on a cloudy day.

sources.claim: Pigeons use sun compass and internal clock
Magnetic sense located in nasal region, linked to trigeminal nerve, demonstrated by magnet experiments
Pigeons use olfactory and visual landmarks for navigation
Magnetic sense can be disrupted with magnets attached to birds
